newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline prices track NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent gasoline prices track NYMEX.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel prices drifted with the underlying NYMEX futures contracts in trade late Wednesday, traders said.

Differentials were largely unaffected by shipping delays on the Houston-to-Chicago Explorer Pipeline system, which pushed liftings back by five days this week following maintenance and a heavy slate of distillate liftings.
"Hopefully, by the end of May we will be back on schedule," Bill Fulton, manager of shipping relations, said. "We will be picking up the rate here in the next few days."
Sources said the Williams pipeline system was accepting additional volumes into the Midwest markets.

"I don't think it's that big of a deal. I think it weakened up the Gulf Coast more than it tightened (the Midcontinent)," one trader active in the Chicago and Group Three markets said of the Explorer delays.
Chicago unleaded gasoline remained 0.25 cent a gallon under to even with NYMEX May unleaded, while Group Three was talked 0.50/0.25 cent under the print, traders said.
Chicago low sulphur diesel bids remained 6.0 cents over NYMEX May heating oil, with Group Three 2.50 cents over the print.
High sulphur was steady at bids 1.50 cents over the print in Chicago and 5.75 cents over the print in Group Three, where traders said lingering agricultural demand was boosting basis.
